title: Hansel and Gretel
summary: Two children get lost in a dark forest and find a strange house.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, two young children named Hansel and Gretel lived near a large forest.
The family had very little food, so times were extremely difficult.
The parents worried constantly about how they will survive the coming winter.
They had no money and almost nothing to eat.
Every single day, the father and mother tried to find a solution.
However, the problem remained very big and serious.
The mother decided that the children must be left deep inside the woods.
She believed this choice was the only way to save the family.
The father felt sad, but he agreed with her plan.
They talked about the idea late into the night.
The children listened quietly from their small bed in the corner.
They felt very afraid of what might happen next.
Hansel thought about a way to keep them safe.
He knew the forest well because he played there often.
When the sun went down, he gathered small white stones along the path.
He put the stones into his pocket and waited for morning.
The next day, the parents took Hansel and Gretel deep into the woods.
As they walked, Hansel dropped the white stones one by one behind him.
The parents left the children alone and walked away quickly.
Hansel and Gretel sat down on the ground and waited for hours.
When the night sky grew dark, the white stones appeared clear and bright.
Those stones helped them find their way back home safely.
Their parents looked surprised when the children returned to the house.
For a short time, the family had peace again.
Unfortunately, the food ran out completely after a few days.
The mother made the same harsh plan once more.
She told the father that they must leave the children again.
This time, Hansel could not gather stones because the door was locked.
The next morning, the family walked far into the forest.
Hansel used small pieces of food instead of stones.
He dropped tiny parts of food along the dark path.
Unluckily, small birds flew down and ate every single piece.
The birds left Hansel and Gretel completely lost in the deep woods.
The brother and sister walked for a long time.
They felt tired, cold, and extremely afraid.
The wind blew through the trees, making strange noises all around them.
They held hands tightly as they moved forward.
Suddenly, the brother and sister discovered a strange house.
The house was made of sweet food like sugar, bread, and chocolate.
They felt very happy because they were extremely empty inside.
As they began to eat the walls, an old woman opened the front door.
She invited them inside with a big smile.
She promised them a wonderful meal and a warm bed for the night.
The children entered the room without any fear.
They sat at a large table and ate as much as they wanted.
After that, the old woman gave them comfortable places to sleep.
However, that old woman was actually a bad person who liked to catch children.
She wanted to cook them and eat them for dinner.
The next morning, she locked Hansel inside a small cage.
She made Gretel work hard every single day.
Gretel had to clean the floors and bring water from the well.
The bad woman planned to cook the boy as soon as he grew fat.
Gretel cried every night because she missed her home and parents.
She hoped that someone would come and save them.
Despite the danger, the young girl remained strong and smart.
She watched the bad woman carefully every single day.
One morning, the woman told Gretel to check the hot oven.
She wanted to bake bread and needed the fire to be very hot.
The smart girl pretended that she did not understand.
She asked the woman to show her how to check the heat.
The bad woman grew angry and leaned inside the hot oven.
As soon as the woman was inside, Gretel pushed her quickly.
Then she closed the heavy door and locked it tight.
The bad woman was completely defeated inside the fire.
Gretel ran fast to the small cage and opened the door for Hansel.
The brother and sister hugged each other with great joy.
They explored the strange house and found a box full of gold coins.
Taking the gold with them, Hansel and Gretel ran happily out of the forest.
They reached a wide water and saw a friendly bird waiting.
The bird carried them across the water safely.
Soon, they saw their small house in the distance.
Their parents were deeply sorry for what they had done.
The family hugged the children and cried tears of joy.
With the gold they brought home, they bought plenty of food.
The parents never left their children again.
Hansel and Gretel grew up healthy and strong.
The family lived together in peace for the rest of their lives.

How did Gretel defeat the wicked witch?
options: She locked her in a cage
She pushed her into the hot oven

sentences.text: Once upon a time, two young children named Hansel and Gretel lived near a large forest with their family.
Because the family had very little food, times were extremely difficult.
The parents worried constantly about how they would survive the coming winter.
They did not know what they should do to feed the children.
Every single day, the situation became worse than it was before.
The mother and father talked about the problem for hours.
They knew that something must be done immediately.
Otherwise, everyone would die because of the lack of food.
The family had very few options left to consider.
Therefore, the parents made a hard decision.
They decided that the children must be left deep inside the woods.
If the children were left alone, the parents might find a way to manage.
This plan was terrible, but the parents felt they had no other choice.
Hansel heard everything that his parents discussed.
He was a smart boy who always planned ahead.
Before they went into the forest, he gathered small white stones along the path.
He put the stones into his pocket quietly.
His parents did not notice what he was doing.
They walked for a long time until they reached a very dark part of the woods.
There, the parents told the children to wait while they gathered wood.
Soon, night came, and the children were completely alone.
When the moon shone brightly, those white stones helped them find their way back home safely.
Their parents were surprised when the children returned.
However, food ran out again very quickly.
The family faced the same terrible problem within days.
The parents decided to leave the children in the woods once more.
This time, they walked even deeper into the forest.
Hansel wanted to gather more stones, but the door was locked.
He could not go outside to find any stones.
Instead, he used pieces of bread which he kept from breakfast.
As they walked, he dropped small pieces of bread on the ground behind them.
He thought that the bread would show them the way home again.
Sadly, many birds flew down from the trees.
Those birds ate the bread pieces completely.
When evening arrived, Hansel and Gretel looked for the bread.
Nothing was left on the ground.
They were completely lost in the dark trees.
While they walked deeper into the forest, they felt tired and cold.
Both the brother and sister were very afraid.
They did not know where they should go.
The wind blew through the trees, making strange noises.
They held each other tightly as they walked through the dark.
They hoped that someone might help them find a safe place.
Suddenly, the brother and sister discovered a strange house.
This house was made entirely of sugar, bread, and sweet chocolate.
They were very empty inside, so they began to eat parts of the walls.
While they ate the sweet walls, an old woman opened the front door.
She looked at them and smiled in a friendly way.
She invited them inside her strange home.
She promised them a wonderful meal and a warm bed for the night.
The children were happy because they were so tired.
They went inside without any fear.
The old woman gave them good food to eat.
After they finished eating, she showed them comfortable beds.
Hansel and Gretel went to sleep quickly.
They believed that they were finally safe.
However, that old woman was actually an evil person who liked to catch children.
She wanted to harm them badly.
The next morning, she showed her true character.
She caught Hansel and locked him inside a small room with iron bars.
Then, she made Gretel work hard every single day.
Gretel had to clean the floors and carry heavy water.
The evil woman planned to cook the boy and eat him for dinner.
She built a big fire under a hot metal container.
Gretel cried every day because she missed her home and her parents.
Despite all the trouble, Gretel remained smart and strong.
She knew she had to find a way to save her brother.
One day, the evil woman asked Gretel to check the hot metal container.
The woman wanted to see if the fire was ready.
The smart girl pretended that she did not understand the instructions.
She told the woman that the opening was too small.
The evil woman became angry at the girl.
She told Gretel that the opening was big enough.
To show the girl how to do it, the evil woman leaned inside the container.
As soon as the woman was inside, Gretel pushed her quickly.
Then, Gretel closed the heavy door and locked it securely.
The evil woman was thus defeated inside her own house.
Gretel ran quickly to open the small room where her brother was kept.
Hansel came out, and both children hugged each other with joy.
They looked around the strange house and found a box full of gold.
Taking the gold with them, Hansel and Gretel ran happily out of the forest.
They walked for hours until they reached a wide river.
They could not cross the water by themselves.
Suddenly, a friendly bird appeared near the water.
The bird let the children sit on its back.
It carried them safely across the wide water.
After they crossed the river, they finally reached their home.
Their parents saw them coming down the road.
The parents were deeply sorry for what they had done.
They cried tears of joy when they hugged their children.
The family promised that they would never separate again.
With the gold they brought from the strange house, they bought all the food they needed.
They never had to worry about winter or hunger again.
The family lived together in peace from that day forward.
Hansel and Gretel grew up healthy and strong.
They often remembered their adventures in the dark forest.
They learned that they could solve any problem if they stayed together.
Their lives changed completely for the better.
The parents treated them with love and care every single day.
Nothing bad ever happened to them again.
The house was always full of laughter and happiness.
People in the village heard the story and visited them often.
The children told everyone about the house made of sugar and chocolate.
No one forgot the lessons they learned during those difficult months.
They lived a long and peaceful life until the very end.

sentences.text: At the edge of a sprawling, ancient forest, a meager cottage sheltered a destitute family of four.
A relentless famine had settled over the land, turning each passing day into a desperate struggle against the encroaching winter.
Inside their damp home, the parents whispered late into the night, wrestling with an unbearable choice.
The mother argued that only by sacrificing the children to the wilderness could the adults hope to survive.
With a heavy heart and a spirit broken by hunger, the father finally yielded to her devastating plan.
Little did the adults know, young Hansel lay awake in the dark, absorbing every harsh word of their conspiracy.
Possessed of a sharp and pragmatic mind, the boy began plotting his defense long before the dawn broke.
As the first pale light filtered through the trees, he slipped into the frosty yard and filled his pockets with luminous white pebbles.
The quartz stones clinked softly against his cotton tunic, reassuring him as the family set out toward the densest part of the woods.
They walked for hours until the canopy overhead choked out the sun, plunging them into a gloomy twilight.
Upon a false pretext of gathering firewood, the parents abandoned the children to the deepening shadows.
Hours bled into the night, leaving Hansel and Gretel shivering and entirely alone in the terrifying stillness.
Yet when the full moon finally climbed above the canopy, its silvery light caught the polished surfaces of Hansel's scattered stones.
Guided by the gleaming trail, the children retraced their steps and arrived home by morning much to their parents' astonishment.
Alas, the meager store of flour vanished almost immediately, plunging the household back into the abyss of starvation.
Once more, the parents resolved to march the children into the uncharted depths of the forest, locking the heavy timber doors to prevent Hansel from collecting stones.
Left with no alternative, the boy saved his morning crust of bread, crumbling the dry heel into tiny fragments as they walked.
With every step deeper into the maze of trunks, he dropped a crumb, trusting the trail to guide them back.
He failed to account for the watchful crows perched high above the branches.
Flocks of hungry birds descended in a silent flurry, devouring every morsel before the shadows could even lengthen.
When evening descended with a freezing wind, the children searched in vain for the reassuring white crumbs.
Lost amidst towering pines that seemed to whisper dark warnings, they huddled together against the biting chill.
Hours blurred into a blur of exhaustion as they stumbled blindly through the underbrush.
Just as despair threatened to consume them, a sudden scent of warm honey and spun sugar drifted through the damp air.
Drawn by the intoxicating aroma, they emerged into a small clearing and stared in absolute wonder.
Rising before them stood a bizarre architectural marvel constructed entirely of gingerbread, frosted glass windows, and rich chocolate tiles.
Overwhelmed by gnawing hunger, the children rushed forward and began to break off pieces of the sweet sugary wall.
Suddenly, a creaking hinge broke the silence as an elderly woman peered out from the heavy oak door.
Wreathed in wrinkles and leaning heavily on a cane, she smiled with practiced warmth and invited them inside.
Promises of pancakes, sugar, apples, and soft feather beds lured the exhausted children across the threshold without a single shred of suspicion.
The gracious hostess fed them a lavish feast before tucking them into crisp, inviting beds where they fell into a profound slumber.
They believed their trials were finally over, little knowing that their sanctuary was a trap spun by a wicked sorceress.
With the first rays of morning, the old woman shed her benevolent facade and revealed her cruel nature.
With surprising strength, she seized Hansel and dragged him to a tiny, iron-barred stable in the yard.
Then she turned her attention to weeping Gretel, forcing the terrified girl into endless drudgery of scrubbing floors and carrying heavy buckets of water.
The witch intended to fatten the boy and roast him for a grand feast, stoking a massive fire beneath a great iron cauldron every single morning.
Gretel wept bitter tears for her brother and her distant home, yet her native cleverness never deserted her.
One afternoon, the impatient hag ordered the girl to check if the roaring oven fire was hot enough to bake bread.
Feigning total ignorance, the smart girl looked up with wide, innocent eyes and declared the opening far too small for her frame.
Exasperated by the delay, the foolish woman snapped that the mouth of the oven was wide enough for anyone.
To demonstrate, the witch thrust her head and shoulders into the roaring heat of the iron chamber.
Seizing the miraculous chance, Gretel lunged forward with all her might and slammed the heavy iron door shut, dropping the heavy latch into place.
The wicked woman shrieked in fury as the heavy metal locked her securely inside her own fiery trap.
Without wasting a single second, Gretel raced across the courtyard and flung open the barred door of the stable.
Hansel burst out into the fresh air, and the siblings fell into each other's arms, weeping tears of pure relief and vindication.
Exploring the strange confectioner's cottage, they discovered heavy chests filled with glittering pearls and heavy gold coins.
Stuffing their pockets with the gleaming treasure, they fled the forest and ran until they reached the banks of a wide, rushing river.
No bridge spanned the churning waters, leaving them stranded until a helpful white duck offered to carry them across one by one.
Safely on the opposite bank, they recognized the familiar rolling hills leading toward their humble village.
As they burst through the cottage door, their repentant parents wept openly, begging for forgiveness and pledging never to abandon them again.
With the boundless wealth they had brought from the forest, poverty became a distant memory and hunger vanished from their lives forever.
The family dwelt together in unbroken harmony, bound by a profound trust that no hardship could ever fracture again.
Hansel and Gretel grew into wise and resilient adults, often gazing toward the distant treeline and remembering the lessons of the dark woods.
No shadow ever touched their threshold again, and their home remained a haven of warmth, laughter, and enduring peace until the end of their days.

quiz.q: How did Hansel manage to return home the first time he and his sister were left in the forest?
options: He followed a trail of white pebbles he had collected in his pockets.
He followed the sound of his mother calling his name.
He dropped pieces of bread that pointed the way back.

quiz.q: Why did Hansel's second attempt to mark the path fail?
options: The wind blew the bread crumbs away into the thick bushes.
Hungry birds flew down and ate every crumb of bread off the ground.
The old woman collected the bread crumbs to feed her pets.

quiz.q: How did Gretel defeat the wicked old woman at the end of the story?
options: She tricked the woman into leaning inside the hot oven and then locked the door.
She pushed the woman into the rushing river while crossing on the duck's back.
She poisoned the woman's morning tea with sugar and chocolate.
